comparison.delta: G04M-R1/R2 dependency-closed memory and ROBDD receipt results are absent from the inspected main tree and open PR summaries; PR #22's Q-LANG entries end at G04L. This is an additive summary, not a claim of scientific novelty.

records.claim: Let K be a finite admitted dependency DAG, with edges from a record to its required records. For an invalidated set B, remove every vertex with a directed path (including a zero-length path) to B. The survivors form the unique greatest dependency-closed subset of K disjoint from B. Indeed, any surviving vertex with a removed dependency would itself reach B; and every dependency-closed subset avoiding B must exclude each vertex reaching B.
records.scope: Fixed graph, fixed record interpretation, no substitution or repair; trusted immutable local state. This is an elementary graph-theoretic property, not an originality or implementation-correctness claim.

verification.independent_finite_check: A separately written set-enumeration and fixed-point calculation on the source's eight-node graph found 24 dependency-closed subsets and checked all 256 invalidation sets; 224 have nonempty survivors. Results match the archived counts. The original implementation was not executed in this intake.

records.scope: Finite fixed-context Boolean expression DAG, n<=12; synthetic local CPU workload; no network or production parser.
records.limitations: Warm API comparison includes the old closure-list construction, but new API trusts immutable admitted records. A direct dictionary is a stronger baseline for exact-repeat lookup. New cold admission is slower. Explicit corruption negative control returns an incorrect count until a full audit detects corruption and clears the store. No persistence, crash recovery, hardware integrity or general speedup demonstrated.
records.verification: Read source results and integrity-checked archive; reported implementation tests and timings not rerun.

records.claim: A fixed-order ROBDD receipt prototype binds the input triple (f,g,p) to the roots, exact counts and union of supports of P=p and Q=p AND (f XOR g). Locally checked dependency-closed receipts can be reused when the trusted context and operands match. Correctness relies on fixed-order ROBDD semantics, collision resistance and intact locally admitted records.
records.limitations: Receiver-only timings exclude proof generation, adapter conversion, actual encoding/decoding, networking and inventory transmission. No independent total-pipeline measurement; stage medians must not be added and labeled a measured total median. Exact-claim cache is substantially faster for exact repeats; unrelated inputs and cold admission can lose. No general speedup, persistence, formal code-correctness or production deployment demonstrated.
records.verification: Source reports inspected and manifest entries checked; no original R2 test execution, timing replication, or formal certificate verification in this intake.

integrity.note: Nested R1's 10 entries duplicate the separately checked R1 manifest; nested parent total also includes H (15) and L (9). Counts are reported separately, not as unique total. Hash matching establishes internal byte consistency only.
